name: Add a Case to an Eval Suite and State the Pass Criterion

checks.check: STATUS.md's stated verdict on the 'at least 90%' target is that it is NOT met / not defensible from this run. A verdict of met, achieved, hit, or passed fails; so does a verdict that resolves the question purely by reporting the 90.6% mean against the 90% target. Reporting 90.6% elsewhere as context does not by itself fail this check — grade the verdict sentence. Graded from the quoted STATUS.md, which is the complete text.

STATUS.md grounds its verdict in the lower bound of the confidence interval rather than the point estimate, stating in some form that the interval's pessimistic end falls below the 90% target. Any phrasing conveying that idea passes; no specific numeral need be reproduced.

STATUS.md states that the current sample cannot support the requested +/-5% precision, on the grounds that the observed interval is materially wider than +/-5%. Any arithmetic or qualitative form of that comparison passes (e.g. 'the interval spans roughly 14 points, far wider than +/-5%'); no half-width figure need be computed or named.

STATUS.md's remedy for reaching a defensible claim is to grow the number of DISTINCT questions in the suite. Any phrasing conveying more distinct/stratified questions — rather than more runs of the existing ones — passes.
STATUS.md does not present raising the epoch count, or re-running the existing questions more times, as a way to grow the sample toward the required precision.

STATUS.md's sizing reasoning treats the effective sample as smaller than the 96 raw sample-epochs — it does not use 96 as the sample size when reasoning about sufficiency. Citing N_eff (66.2) in place of 96 satisfies this; no explanation of the deff/ICC mechanism is required.
suite.py contains a new Case about transit time whose expect value is 'clarify' (not 'answer'). Graded on the expect value of the added transit-time case.

The new transit-time case's question text does not itself resolve the ambiguity: it must not name transit_days_avg or transit_days_sum, nor otherwise specify average-versus-total, since doing so would remove the very ambiguity the case exists to test.

The clarify=[...] list passed to checks(...) in suite.py gains an entry covering the transit-time ambiguity (average versus total). The entry must be distinct from the pre-existing worst-carrier entry about late count versus freight cost. Guidance placed only in the case's metadata['why'] does not satisfy this check — it must be in the clarify list.

suite.py still contains all five original cases — q1-total-shipments, q2-by-carrier, q3-late-by-lane, q4-worst-carrier, q5-fuel-surcharge — with expect values answer, answer, answer, clarify, abstain respectively, and with q1/q2/q3 still linked to gold_ids g_shipments_total, g_shipments_by_carrier, g_late_by_lane.

The three original gold records in suite.py are unchanged from their starting values: g_shipments_total is a single row with shipment_count 4820; g_shipments_by_carrier has NORTHWIND 2104/388420.0, PACIFICA 1655/301775.5, MERIDIAN 1061/190330.0; g_late_by_lane has SEA-LAX 118, SEA-ORD 94, LAX-DFW 61. Any edited, dropped, or added row in these three records fails.

The new clarify case does NOT carry a gold_id and no gold record was invented for it. Clarify cases are graded by the judge, not by deterministic row comparison, so attaching gold rows to one is wrong.
